correctness.rationale: For every finite field F_q including characteristic 2, derivations have D(v+cz)=Av+(ell(v)+tr(A)c)z and automorphisms T(v+cz)=Av+(ell(v)+det(A)c)z with A invertible. Pairwise interpolation forces field-homogeneous quotient map f, homogeneous central map g; for automorphisms f induces a projective permutation and nonzero images, g has nonzero central multiplier and permutation on every nonzero quotient vertical fibre. Conversely, independently selected witnesses interpolate each pair: independent quotient vectors determine A and allow arbitrary ell, while dependent quotients with independent whole elements prescribe a trace or nonzero determinant via (g(tv,d)-t*g(v,c))/(d-tc). This establishes the all-q iff classification, including q=2. Homogeneous-map enumeration yields q^(q^2+3q+3) derivations, and (q+1)!(q-1)^(q+2)(q!)^(q+1) automorphisms. Independently constructed every ordinary F2 witness (64 derivations, 24 automorphisms) and checked every pair for ALL 8192 homogeneous two-local derivation candidates and ALL 48 classified automorphism candidates. These tests confirm finite cases; pair-witness proof supports arbitrary finite q.

originality.rationale: Ayupov–Kudaybergenov 2016 full text Theorem 3.1 constructs nonordinary two-local automorphisms on broad nilpotent Lie algebras from homogeneous central functions. Ayupov/Kudaybergenov/Rakhimov 2015 already construct nonordinary two-local derivations, and Sheng/Liu/Miao 2025 explicitly study LINEAR two-local automorphisms of Heisenberg algebras. Thus existence and linear subcases are known. The full arbitrary-map finite-field iff classification, projective quotient permutations, vertical-fibre permutations and exact q-dependent cardinalities were not found in these sources. Full 2025 Heisenberg paper unavailable; prior coverage remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: Classifying *all* nonlinear two-local derivations and automorphisms over every finite field, with explicit q-dependent counts, gives a complete natural local-to-global obstruction census in the smallest nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra. It quantifies genuinely nonlinear examples far beyond existence constructions and includes the characteristic-two boundary. This is a structural classification, not just known isolated examples.
